question: A 55-year-old woman, type 2 diabetic and obese, on treatment with metformin, with 8% Hb A1c, tells a story of recurrent urinary tract infections. Which of the following therapeutic options to associate with metformin considers the LESS adequate?
analysis: In this case, the patient is a 55-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs). Among the options provided, SGLT2 inhibitors are known to increase the risk of urinary tract infections due to their mechanism of action, which promotes glucose excretion in the urine. Therefore, adding an SGLT2 inhibitor to her treatment regimen would be the least adequate choice considering her history of recurrent UTIs. DPP4 inhibitors, GLP1 analogs, and basal insulin do not have a similar association with UTIs.
